prompt: The query in the editor has one mistake. Fix it so that it answers this question: what new MRR did LedgerLoop book in each month of 2025 (event_date from 1 January to 31 December 2025), in euros rounded to 2 decimals with ROUND? Each event's event_type names its movement (new, expansion, contraction, churn or reactivation); a reactivation is an account coming back after it churned, never new MRR. Leave out the opening events: they carry the MRR subscriptions already had when the data starts on 1 January 2024. Convert every amount to euros at one fixed rate, that of 31 December 2025: multiply by fx_rates.eur_per_unit for the subscription's currency on 2025-12-31. Count an event in the month of its event_date. Return two columns, in this order: month_start (the first day of the month) and new_mrr. Return one row for each month with new MRR. Any row order is fine.
hints: Next, check which event types the filter keeps: is every one of them new business?
A reactivation is an account that churned and came back, so its MRR is not new MRR.
starter_sql:
SELECT CAST(date_trunc('month', e.event_date) AS DATE) AS month_start,
  ROUND(SUM(e.mrr_delta_local * f.eur_per_unit), 2) AS new_mrr
FROM subscription_events e
JOIN subscriptions s ON s.subscription_id = e.subscription_id
JOIN fx_rates f ON f.currency = s.currency AND f.rate_date = DATE '2025-12-31'
WHERE e.event_type IN ('new', 'reactivation')
  AND e.event_date BETWEEN DATE '2025-01-01' AND DATE '2025-12-31'
GROUP BY CAST(date_trunc('month', e.event_date) AS DATE)
why_this_works: Keeping only new events books returning accounts as reactivations, so new MRR is not inflated by won-back customers.
